title: Nintendo Said No to Xenoblade in America. Fans Changed Its Mind
hook:
In June 2011 Nintendo of America said it had no plans to release Xenoblade Chronicles in the US, so fans launched Operation Rainfall and six months later Nintendo gave in. This week Xenoblade Chronicles 3 got its update ahead of the Switch 2 Edition on December 3. Would Xenoblade exist in the West without that fan campaign?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Nintendo of America once refused to release Xenoblade Chronicles in the United States? The game came out in Japan in June of twenty ten on the Wii, and Europe got it as well. But in June of twenty eleven, Nintendo of America said it had no plans to bring it to the States. Fans would not accept that. They started a campaign called Operation Rainfall and flooded Nintendo with emails, phone calls and social media posts. They asked for three Wii role playing games: Xenoblade Chronicles, The Last Story and Pandora's Tower. On December second, twenty eleven, Nintendo gave in and announced Xenoblade Chronicles for North America. It finally launched in North America in April of twenty twelve. You could only buy it at GameStop stores, on GameStop's website, or straight from Nintendo's own online store. That small release grew into one of Nintendo's best known role playing series. And this week Xenoblade Chronicles Three got its version three point zero update. It prepares the game for the Nintendo Switch Two Edition arriving on December third. That edition adds a new hero named Shimmer, a mode called Heroes' Vault, and sixty frames per second. Would Xenoblade exist in the West without that fan campaign? Follow for more gaming history.
